newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Cariplo sees Bourse float in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Cariplo sees Bourse float in 1997.

text.p: Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo is hoping for a stock market flotation this year after parliament approves a decree law reorganising bank foundations, chairman Sandro Molinari said.
Molinari told reporters attending a business conference that once the law is passed Cariplo would be able to seek a listing. "I hope this will be in 1997," he said.
Legislation to reorganise the status of the foundations which control many of Italy's big banks is currently going through parliament.
The foundation of Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde, Cariplo's sole shareholder, said last year it was ready to sell a stake, and even a majority stake, in the bank.
The company pulled plans for a partial flotation in the summer of 1994 blaming adverse market conditions.

The two Cariplo-controlled troubled southern Italian savings banks, Caripuglia and Carical, on whose rescue the bank has spent nearly 2.0 trillion lire, should not affect Cariplo's planned privatisation, Molinari said.

"It is the Cariplo group going for a bourse listing and these two banks are part of the group. We have restored them to health without touching our assets and all this was charged on the 1996 accounts," he added.
